clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3. What the docs and public source say about the producer's compiler, and what the only public MegaETH compiler computes for MULMOD, SAR, SHL, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD and CALLDATALOAD, with constant operands at pcs 22378, 22639, 15519, 16642 and 12232.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched aot_instructions.hpp and aot_execution_state.hpp from megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler branch aot-compiler (HTTP 200). The handlers read as the item says: mulmod writes stack[2] without a pop, signextend builds its mask as 1u << (b-1), byte shifts by a byte index, sar tests x < 0 on uint256, which is unsigned _BitInt(256), and get_jumpdest returns the entry from lower_bound without checking that the key equals the target. src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:61-70 unpacks every BalanceDelta with sar(128) and signextend(15), and one side of an ordinary swap is negative, so these handlers would change mined amounts and state roots in ordinary blocks. The item's conclusion that the producer does not run them rests on the validator reproducing those blocks, which I did not rerun. A replica eth_call of SAR(128, -5) on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc returned all ones, the specified result. The item is right that this speaks for the replica and not for the producer.

clearedSpotChecks.check: mega-evm v1.7.3 added discard_tx and discard_transaction for a transaction whose execution panicked. Without them, an embedder that catches the panic and reuses the EVM keeps the panicked transaction's state writes, logs, transient storage, memory and frames.
clearedSpotChecks.note: mega-evm v1.7.4 crates/mega-evm/src/evm/mod.rs lines 394-440 says a panic skips cleanup and that discard_tx finalizes the journal, which clears transient storage, logs and warm sets. On the code side, unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) reverts at entry if the lock flag is set and checks NonzeroDeltaCount before it locks again, and the flag lives in transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27). A leaked flag from a panicked transaction would let another sender's calls pass onlyWhenUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99) without an unlock frame of their own. That needs the producer to catch a panic and reuse the EVM, and no panic input an ordinary account can send is known. So the item is correctly left as a lead, and no on-chain trace of it was found. I did not rerun the census of cycle 18.
